newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- World Food Programme grants Morocco $16 million for school canteens on condition there will be new management.
- Casablanca Stock Exchange still bullish amid mounting worries that inflated prices do not reflect real value of stocks.

- Despite delayed rains, main economic sectors seem to be on right track. Electricity output is going up, cement sector is rallying after years of decline. Finance Ministry figures show foreign investment increased in January.

- Othman Benjelloun, managing director of Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur attributes bank's good results in 1996 to better management and success of Global Depositary Receipts which he says continue to draw interest of foreign investors.

- Negative weather conditions hamper economic growth as inadequate government policy deepens crisis with each drought season. Instead of increasing subsidies and devising special budgets, it would be better to develop small and medium-sized agro-industry firms to curb rural migration.
